title: Freshfields and Anthropic Team Up to Co-Build AI Legal Workflows, Deploying Claude Across the Firm Globally
author: Freshfields · Anthropic

dom.t: Model providers: Suppliers now compete for workflows

st.t: Model providers: Suppliers now compete for workflows
st.an: The announcement materially extends the cluster’s proposition with a concrete global-law-firm example: Anthropic is not merely supplying a model but jointly developing agentic legal workflows, while Claude is embedded within Freshfields’ proprietary, institutionally grounded platform. The CoCounsel integration also supports the cluster’s supplier–partner structure. Claimed service improvements remain anticipated rather than independently measured, and the source does not establish specialist-vendor displacement.
qs: In parallel, Freshfields and Anthropic have established a unique co-development program to build legal-focused AI applications and design agentic workflows to enable faster and more efficient delivery of legal advice to clients.

kp.k: Claude access expands across Freshfields’ global workforce
kp.d: The April 23, 2026 announcement reports that Freshfields has provided Claude access to 5,700 employees through its proprietary AI platform and uses Claude daily on client matters. It reports adoption and usage increasing by ~500 percent within the first six weeks, without specifying separate measures or starting levels. The multi-year agreement commits to global deployment across 33 offices, covering all practice groups and business services.
qs: Freshfields uses Claude daily on client matters via the firm’s AI platform serving 5,700 users.
Within the first six weeks, the adoption and usage of Claude has increased by ~500 percent, with thousands of users leveraging Freshfields’ solutions to access Claude.
The collaboration includes a commitment to firmwide deployment of the Claude suite of products and frontier AI models globally across 33 offices, spanning all practice groups and business services.

kp.k: Law firm and client legal team co-design workflows
kp.d: Over the next 12 months, Freshfields and Anthropic’s in-house legal teams plan to define new AI workflows and processes for providing legal services to Anthropic. Separately, an established co-development program will build legal-focused applications and agentic workflows for client advice. These are announced development plans rather than reported outcomes.
qs: Over the next 12 months, Freshfields and Anthropic’s in-house legal teams plan to collaborate and define new AI workflows and processes leveraging Anthropic tools and solutions' latest capabilities to deliver legal services for Anthropic.

In parallel, Freshfields and Anthropic have established a unique co-development program to build legal-focused AI applications and design agentic workflows to enable faster and more efficient delivery of legal advice to clients.

kp.k: AI development targets legal tasks and business services
kp.d: The stated focus encompasses legal and market research, contract review, drafting, due diligence, business-services automation, and multi-step legal tasks. Freshfields Lab co-head Gerrit Beckhaus describes the intended agentic workflows as handling multi-step tasks end-to-end and predicts faster, more precise and more scalable services; the announcement provides no measured performance results for these anticipated benefits.
qs: Contract review, document drafting and due diligence
Agentic workflows for multi-step legal tasks

With this collaboration, we are going further: co-developing agentic workflows with Anthropic that can handle multi-step legal tasks end-to-end. For our clients, that translates into faster, more precise and more scalable legal services.

kp.k: Proprietary platforms connect AI with institutional knowledge
kp.d: The announcement describes existing Freshfields Lab platforms integrating Claude as a common access point for lawyers and business-services professionals, connected to the firm’s institutional knowledge. Further embedding Claude’s reasoning and jointly developed agentic workflows in general-purpose tools is presented as the collaboration’s next step.
qs: Through the Freshfields Lab, the firm has developed proprietary platform solutions that integrate Claude, giving every lawyer and business services professional a single, secure entry point to AI-powered workflows connected to the firm’s institutional knowledge.
This collaboration will embed Claude’s reasoning capabilities into general-purpose AI tools across the firm, including agentic workflows built jointly with Anthropic.

kp.k: Agentic expansion is tied to governance and training
kp.d: Freshfields plans to expand to Anthropic’s Cowork agentic platform in line with its security, compliance and training frameworks. Chief Innovation Officer Gil Perez frames adoption around practical client outcomes and responsibility and governance; these are stated deployment principles, not evidence of particular safeguards or their effectiveness.
qs: Freshfields plans to expand to Cowork, Anthropic's agentic AI platform, in line with the firm's security, compliance, and training frameworks.
For us, innovation is about practical impact – helping our teams deliver the very best outcomes for clients, while holding ourselves to the highest standards of responsibility and governance,

kp.k: Partnership combines early model access with legal-tool testing
kp.d: Freshfields will receive early access to future Anthropic models and tools. The announcement also reports that the firm is already adopting and testing the next generation of Thomson Reuters’ CoCounsel Legal, rebuilt using Anthropic technology and incorporating Westlaw and Practical Law. This distinguishes proprietary platform development from adoption of a third-party legal product.
qs: The firm will receive early access to future Anthropic models and tools to better serve clients.

Freshfields is also an early adopter and tester of Thomson Reuters' next generation of CoCounsel Legal – fully rebuilt using Anthropic’s latest technology, with Westlaw and Practical Law natively embedded.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Freshfields and Anthropic report existing daily use of Claude on client matters and expanding firm-wide adoption through Freshfields’ proprietary AI platform.
pts.d: The joint announcement says Claude is available to 5,700 employees and that adoption and usage increased by approximately 500 percent within the first six weeks. It distinguishes this existing access from a commitment to deploy the Claude suite globally across 33 offices, all practice groups and business services. The platform connects AI-powered workflows to the firm’s institutional knowledge.

pts.k: The partners plan to co-develop AI-native legal services and agentic workflows; Freshfields Lab co-head Gerrit Beckhaus predicts end-to-end handling of multi-step tasks and faster, more precise, scalable services.
pts.d: The announcement describes planned collaboration with Anthropic’s in-house legal team on services delivered to Anthropic and a parallel co-development program for legal applications and agentic workflows. Target activities include legal and market research, contract review, drafting, due diligence and business-services automation. Beckhaus attributes prospective client benefits to workflows that handle multi-step legal tasks end-to-end. The source does not specify the degree of human supervision or claim that lawyers will be replaced.

pts.k: Freshfields’ Gil Perez frames the partnership as accelerating responsible client-focused innovation; Anthropic’s Kate Jensen interprets the deployment as a wider professional-services adoption milestone.
pts.d: Perez says the partnership strengthens Freshfields’ ability to co-innovate quickly while introducing secure and compliant capabilities. Jensen makes the broader market interpretation that Freshfields’ adoption across legal work, business services and agentic workflows signals the arrival of enterprise AI in professional services. This is Jensen’s interpretation, not a separately measured market-wide finding.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The source offers internal adoption figures, deployment experience and executive testimony, but no measured service-performance results.
pts.d: The announcement’s quantitative support consists of access for 5,700 employees, thousands of users and approximately 500 percent growth in adoption and usage over six weeks. It does not define the growth metric or provide its baseline. Existing platform integration, Beckhaus’s account of Claude’s role in proprietary solutions and early testing of CoCounsel Legal supply experiential support. Faster, more precise, efficient and scalable services are asserted or anticipated without benchmarks, client case results, quantified time savings or accuracy measurements. Jensen’s sector-wide interpretation rests on Freshfields’ deployment decision.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The April 23, 2026 announcement separates current use from a multi-year agreement and a next-12-month workflow collaboration, with expansion subject to firm governance frameworks.
pts.d: Daily use, platform access and the first-six-week adoption increase are presented as existing developments at publication. The agreement is multi-year; collaboration between the legal teams to define workflows for serving Anthropic is planned over the next 12 months. Early access to future models is promised, while expansion to Cowork is planned in line with security, compliance and training frameworks. No completion date is specified for firm-wide suite deployment or realization of the predicted speed, precision and scalability benefits.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The direct scope is Freshfields’ lawyers and business-services staff worldwide, its clients, and Anthropic as both technology collaborator and legal-services client.
pts.d: Freshfields’ employees across 33 offices and all practice groups are intended users of the expanded AI tools. Lawyers’ research, review, drafting and due-diligence workflows are targeted alongside business-services automation. Clients are promised faster, more precise, scalable advice. Anthropic’s in-house legal team participates on the buyer side in redesigning services delivered to Anthropic, while its product teams collaborate on applications and workflows. Jensen extends the significance to professional services generally. The document makes no specific claims about staffing reductions, fees, entry-level employment or access to justice.
